Sam Altman supports Induced AI, an AI startup founded by two teenagers. Google unveiled the Pixel 8 and Pixel 8 Pro, highlighting improvements in cameras, screen brightness, and AI features. Dave Clark, former CEO of Flexport, resigned and criticized the founder and board. According to a book by Michael Lewis, Sam Bankman-Fried attempted to bribe Donald Trump. Google implemented stricter spam policies for Gmail, requiring authentication and limiting reported spam. TikTok is testing an ad-free subscription tier. LinkedIn introduced AI features in job hunting, marketing, and sales products. Elon Musk confirmed contradictory metrics on X Platform usage, stating 100-200 million daily posts but later claiming 500 million. IronNet, founded by a former NSA director, closed down and laid off its staff due to financial failure and lack of market traction.

# See also

* [Google's AI Practices and Antitrust Suit Against News Publishers](../ai-litigation/google-s-ai-practices-and-antitrust-suit-against-news.md) - A class action lawsuit filed by news publishers accuses Google and Alphabet of anticompetitive practices, particularly regarding AI technologies used in Google's Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot. The lawsuit alleges misuse of publishers' content and ad revenue, and seeks an injunction to prevent improper use of publisher data for AI training.
* [Sam Bankman-Fried's Character Portrayal and Defense Strategies](../ai-defense-law/sam-bankman-fried-s-character-portrayal-and-defense.md) - This note captures the contrasting narratives presented in the source regarding Sam Bankman-Fried's character and actions. It includes the defense's portrayal of Alameda Research and FTX, the use of the 'building a plane' analogy, and testimonies from Marc-Antoine Julliard and Adam Yedidia.
* [Sam Bankman-Fried's Financial and Political Interactions](../crypto-crises/sam-bankman-fried-s-financial-and-political-interactions.md) - This note covers Sam Bankman-Fried's interactions with Michael Lewis, his meetings with political figures, and the collapse of FTX. It includes discussions about offering $5 billion to Donald Trump and the negative perception of him after the FTX collapse.

<note>
- Google's search product is favored by users, browsers, and device makers due to its perceived excellence.
- Changing from Google Search to another provider can be inconvenient due to the lack of familiarity with new search results.
- Users often revert to Google after setting up a new device or browser, indicating a preference for Google.
- Google's dominance is partly attributed to its scale, longevity, and user data collection, which no other competitor can match.
- Allegations of Google manipulating search queries for maximum ad revenue have been denied by the company.
- Discusses the increase in data volume and the changes in search behavior over time.
</note>

* [Apple's Defense of Google Search Deal in Court](../ai-litigation/apple-s-defense-of-google-search-deal-in-court.md) - Apple's defense in the US v. Google antitrust trial includes arguments about user experience, privacy, and the necessity of Google's services in Apple's ecosystem.

In 2018, Google made a proposal to preinstall Google services on every iOS device, which would have allowed Google to collect more data and potentially increase revenue. This move was seen as a way to strengthen Google's position in the search market. However, Apple rejected the idea, citing concerns about user privacy and control over their devices.
